note: WHICH COLUMNS HAVE ACTUALLY BEEN READ AT MIGNE'S PLATE. Written 2026-08-28, the day 9003's full collation showed our Corpus Corporum Latin departs from the plate at ~3 sites per page against a standing corpus estimate of THREE INSTANCES IN TOTAL. This file exists so that `scripts/plate-gate.mjs` can refuse a [sic:] or a [var:] on a column nobody has read. It records READS, not findings: a range belongs here when someone put the page on screen, read the corner numbers first, and read the running text -- whether or not anything was found. Its opposite number is data/plate-notes/coverage.json, which records only the foot-of-page conjecture layer. || 2026-08-29: extended by the [sic:] plate sweep across PL 113/114/202 — 56 pages, 80 markers, ledger at data/plate-sweep/2026-08-29-sic-sweep.tsv. ⛔ 8988 col 0636A is DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED: the page was read, but the word (aurursus / aut / au) sits in the extreme right margin where that scan has ink bleed and could not be resolved. Leaving it unrecorded keeps the gate flagging that marker, which is the honest state — a read that could not settle the word is not a read for this purpose.
why_the_gate: A [sic:] asserts a defect in MIGNE'S TYPE and a [var:] asserts that MIGNE'S TEXT diverges from a scriptural witness. Both are public claims about the printed page. Our Latin is not the printed page -- it is Corpus Corporum's transcription of it -- so neither claim can be licensed by the file alone. Corpus frequency detects that an error EXISTS; it cannot say WHOSE it is (reference_plate-read-triage.md). Vulgate collation is worse than useless for the [var:] class: 9003 @0763D showed the digitization MANUFACTURING a divergence (judicabit -> judicavit) that the collation then dutifully 'found'.
rule: NOT A RETROFIT (CLAUDE.md, "RECOVER GOING FORWARD, DO NOT SWEEP THE DONE CORPUS"). The gate is a SHIP TEST: run it on a work before marking it `ours`. Works shipped before 2026-08-28 are surveyed by `--all`, which measures the exposure and exits zero; the number it prints is evidence for a decision about sample width, not a mandate to re-open 38 books.

fields.from/to: inclusive column range, banded (0719A) or bare (0719). A read of one PDF page covers TWO columns, i.e. all eight bands A-D of both.
fields.depth: 'full' = the running text of every column in the range was collated word by word against our Latin. 'read' = the page was read at the plate for a named question and the surrounding text scanned, but not collated word by word. Only 'full' licenses silence about a column; both license a marker, because both mean a human eye met the type.
fields.source: scan identifier + page map + the calibration actually performed. A page map asserted but not calibrated against printed corner numbers is not a source.

8967.scan_defect: INNER-MARGIN CLIPPING: on SOME leaves the left-hand column loses 3-5 characters at the start of most lines (`VERS.` prints as `s.`). ⛔⛔ IT IS SPORADIC AND CANNOT BE PREDICTED FROM THE COLUMN NUMBER. Open the column; never infer. || HISTORY, because the claim was wrong TWICE and each retreat was forced by more reading. (1) At chunking I stated a RULE from five pages: a left-hand column numbered 1 (mod 4) is clipped. (2) Refuted at col 901, and I retreated to 'a strong tendency, 5 of 6'. (3) THAT WAS ALSO WRONG, and by then it was wrong in a way five pages could not have shown. With the reads from cols 0850-0870 in, mod-1 columns stand at 5 CLIPPED (841, 849, 893, 897, 1045) against 6 CLEAN (853, 857, 861, 865, 869, 901). That is a coin flip, not a tendency. ⚑ THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE SAMPLE, NOT THE SCANNER: my five pages were four consecutive leaves plus one, so they sampled one region of one physical gathering and the congruence was an artifact of contiguity. A pattern found in a contiguous sample is a pattern OF THAT SAMPLE until it is tested somewhere else. ⚑ AND THE FAILURE MODE RUNS WHERE NOBODY AUDITS: a wrong 'clipped' does not ship a bad marker, it silently WITHHOLDS a good one and leaves no artifact behind. It blocked three legitimate candidates in cols 0892-0901 before a stint opened the page. || WHAT STANDS: where a column IS actually clipped and a marker rests on a line-opening word, it needs a second copy (Gallica; data/volumes.json) before it may ship.
8967.normalization_class: Corpus Corporum silently conforms Migne's text to the Vulgate. ⛔ INVISIBLE TO EVERY CHECK WE RUN: a Vulgate collation cannot see it, because the digitization has already made Migne agree with the Vulgate. The mirror of the [var:] hazard the runbook records -- there collation MANUFACTURES a divergence, here it DESTROYS one. Only the plate reaches it. Confirmed and patched: 0847A sordescet (TEI had the Clementine's sordescat). Reported, patches pending: 0899B audiebant (TEI has audiebam = Clementine), 0895A populus (TEI has populis), 0866D the TEI INSERTS `vel` before `adipem` (the only one so far that touches sense). Also the hyphenation artifact 0853B de-cidam (TEI has the non-word deeidam). ⭐⭐ AND THE CLASS MUST NOT BE APPLIED BY ANALOGY, which was tested rather than assumed: a SECOND `sordescat` stands at 0869A, and when that leaf was read it prints `sordescat` -- agreeing with our TEI. Patching the twin site by inference would have corrupted Migne's own text into a reading he never printed. Our copy cannot arbitrate this class anywhere.

8999.caveat: ⛔ LEAF n215'S PRINTED RIGHT-HAND CORNER READS 421, NOT 420. Verified at 6x. n216 then reads 421/422, so 421 IS PRINTED TWICE IN PL 114 AND 420 IS NEVER PRINTED -- Migne's compositor mis-numbered the leaf. The running text settles it (n215-right runs VERS. 37 Tu dicis -> Sicut agnus coram tondente, and n216-left opens with that sentence's continuation, our [0421A]), so n215-right IS column 420 and is recorded as such. A reader trusting corner numbers alone would misfile every finding on that column by one. ⚑ ALSO: a <pb> ANCHOR IS NOT A LOCATOR FOR A PHRASE NEAR IT. Four sites in this work sit in a different band from the anchor that precedes them -- actionem personarum is at 386D not 0387A, the [cj:] nobis at 414D not 0415A, liberatum at 0420A not 0420B, Separatur at 0422B not 0422A. This is CLAUDE.md's band-arithmetic false positive seen from the other side and is NOT a defect: the anchors are transcribed where Migne sets them. Nothing was patched.

9000.note: 2026-09-04. All 33 [var:] of 9000 read at the plate across 22 leaves, BEFORE the work shipped: 32 confirmed as Migne's own printing, 1 withdrawn (0307B confusus -> confessus). ⭐ 12 of the 17 TEI patches came from the stints' DECLINED-ODDITY lists or from reading a page opened for something else -- not one from a fired marker, which is John's finding reproduced. FIVE ARE SILENT REPAIRS (CC tidying a defect Migne printed): quator, propetiae lectonis, invenitur- Qoud, sapipientiae, astritus -- the class no collation can reach, because the digitization removed the evidence first; two of them were in no stint's list at all. ⭐⭐ 0330A CONFIRMED AND IT IS A REAL EDITORIAL FINDING: the plate prints Gloria in EXCELSIS Deo at Luke 2:14 and gloria in excelsis again two lines later at Luke 19:38, so Migne (or his source) conformed the nativity song to the entry song the gloss is expounding on that same page. ⚠ SCAN DEFECTS RECORDED FOR THE VOLUME: leaf n153's left corner is set '9 5' (the medial 9 of 295 is a dropped sort), beside the known n215 mis-numbering where 421 prints twice and 420 never. ⚠ The reads are TARGETED, not word-by-word over every column: one reader found in altera species / specie while checking something else and said plainly that a full pass would turn up more of that class. Full account in src/english/9000/cruces.md §9.

reads.found: Work division page: five stub entries and PROPHETIA BARUCH close above a full-width rule, Matthew opens below it. The asterisk-keyed foot note on this page belongs to Baruch (8996) and was NOT adopted. No foot-of-page apparatus belonging to Matthew. Archive prints 'ad memorian reliquit'; GALLICA PRINTS 'memoriam' and our twin agrees -- archive-only, refuted, no marker.

Running head confirmed 'GLOSSA ORDINARIA. -- EVANG. MATTH.' FOUR archive-only candidates, ALL REFUTED BY GALLICA, our twin right at each: 'sa cramentum' (split type) vs sacramentum; 'Aminabad' vs Aminadab; 'Eclesiam' vs Ecclesiam; 'ei novissima mors' vs 'et'. Two further archive-only oddities also refuted: 'gentes Domini' (Gallica and Ps 112:4 read Dominus) and 'incipit ad exordio' (Gallica reads 'ab exordio').

CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES: 'alter in principio sequentis. Sed mystice' -- Migne prints a FULL STOP after sequentis which our twin has lost. TEI patch filed. Gallica's 'tesseratlecadis' is ink; the archive prints tesseradecadis, as our twin does. Archive prints 'generandus.' with a terminal stop at 0067A where Gallica and our twin have none -- archive-only, declined.

Both witnesses confirm the two readings a [var:] rests on: 'Ipse invocavit me' (0069A, perfect for the Vulgate's future invocabit) and 'Ecce Deus adjuvit me' (0069B, perfect for the Vulgate's present adjuvat, beside Migne's own etymology 'Adjutus'). THREE archive-only oddities refuted by Gallica, our twin right at each: 'ressuscitans' vs resuscitans; 'Mathan, qui per Solomonen descendit' vs 'Salomonem'; 'suspicio lector.' vs 'lectori'. Both witnesses confirm the doubled 'Non quod postea convenerint' at 0070C -- it is Migne's, and the two copies have distinct continuations, so it is a splice of two glosses, not an eye-skip.

CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES: 'sic prophetia non necessitatem EORUM facit' at 0071D, where our twin prints the non-word 'oerum'. Corpus Corporum's corruption; TEI patch filed; the English renders eorum per the PLATE-WHERE-READ rule. Nothing else divergent on either column.

PRESS VARIANT, and the only one in the range: at 0073A Gallica prints the lemma 'Bethehem Judae' (no l) and the ARCHIVE prints 'Bethlehem Judae'. Both are clean, legible, normally spaced; the very next line of both copies prints Bethlehem correctly three times. Our twin follows Gallica's printing. NO [sic:] -- it fails the two-witness bar in the same way 8950 @0171D Mititte/Mittite did. Also confirmed on both: 'Explorabat etiam, si rex eorum', 'Rex injustus omnes ministros impios habet' with injustus set in ROMAN between Migne's italics.

CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES: 'incepit in eum PERSECUTIO' at 0076C, where our twin prints the non-word 'pesecutio'. Corpus Corporum's corruption; TEI patch filed. Both witnesses confirm 'Puer natus est nobis' at 0075B (the [var:] on Isa 9:6 Parvulus) and 'quem actum esse hominem intelligunt' at 0075B (a real word, rendered as printed, crux logged). Archive-only and refuted: 'Ex Aegypto, vocavi' with a comma (Gallica and our twin have none); 'VERS. 11. --' with a dash (Gallica and our twin have none). Gallica f38 is faint and foxed but legible throughout.

TWO archive-only candidates refuted by Gallica, our twin right at both: 'flere dicat ur' (split type) vs dicatur; 'Helia et Henoch' vs Enoch. Gallica also refutes the archive's 'Juaedorum' (ink). Both witnesses confirm 'ideo Josephus intellexit Judaeam' at 0077D -- a real word, rendered as printed, crux logged. Both confirm the direct question already set behind a colon at 0078B ('Quaeritur: quare non timuit...?'), so Pattern 8b needed no recasting.

Targeted re-read at 400 dpi (archive) and native-resolution IIIF crop (Gallica), raised by the blind polarity reader of chunks 0000-0010. BOTH COPIES PRINT `dum parit, justitiam habet` -- so the reading is MIGNE'S, not the digitization's, and our Latin carries it verbatim, which is what makes a [sic:] writable at all. It is a defect: the allusion is Jo 16:21 *mulier cum parit TRISTITIAM habet*, and Migne's own next clause on the same two lines prints *Tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium (Joan. XVI)* -- the contradicting neighbour is four words away in his own type. [sic: justitiam] fired; the English keeps the literal 'she has justice' per 7a. ⚑ Incidentally confirms the 0000-0005 stint's `Henoch`/`Enoch` refutation on this same page: archive prints Henoch, Gallica Enoch.

reads.ruling: DECLINED under launch-brief §2, which lets a single-word [var:] stand only where the gloss argues from the word or the form is one letter-level corruption cannot manufacture. Limb 1 fails: the gloss says only 'Geraza urbs est Arabiae' and leans on nothing in the letter. Limb 2 is satisfied as to OWNERSHIP but that is not the same as materiality: this is the form of a transliterated place-name, the class the 0000-0005 stint declined five times under its Policy 4 (Esrom, Josaphat, Eliachim, Sadoch, Nazareus). Γερασηνῶν has no settled Latin transliteration and the English is the same word either way. ⚑ Recorded as arguable: unlike Nazareus, Migne does NOT vary within his own column here, and uniformity is the harder case; the decline rests on reading a consistent orthography as house style rather than as a reading.

(1) 0211A CONFIRMED, and it is the control for the 0210D [var:]: eleven lines below the broken reading, Migne sets the SAME VERSE CORRECTLY -- 'deterret dicens Rom. IX : O homo, quis es qui respondeas Deo.' Two columns, two crops, two distinct readings of Rom 9:20 by the same compositor. Note the terminal FULL STOP, not a question mark; Pattern 8 keeps it. (2) 0211A CONFIRMED, a [var:] site: '(RAB.) Septimum praeceptum : Non furaberis;' -- Migne's wording is Rom 13:9's, not Ex 20:15's 'Non furtum facies'. ALSO CONFIRMED AS PRINTED: the bracketed variant 'curiosius [curiosus]' in roman brackets; 'Et audivit arcana verba, quae non licet homini loqui'; '(AUG., quaest. 35 in Exod., tom. III.)'; 'ne jumenta interirent omnia'; 'Mosem non juberi omnia miranda facere virga'; the bracketed variant 'Mosi [Moses]' at 0212B; 'nec dicitur quod intraverint Moses et Aaron ad eum ... et non poterant resistere Mosi'; 'nec intrat, sed vocatur ad Pharaonem'.
